question.problem: Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -3 & -6\end{aligned}]$ and the quadratic curve ${x}^{T}\,Ax=3.$ Given that $A$ has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-7,$ find the principal axes of the curve.

current_example.problem: Consider the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/ab05d1710aec56c3ccd3bed1bf93b0fb3a481111b907dd4a48158c9f6e9d5d48.svg) and the quadratic curve $\mathbf{x}^T \! A \mathbf{x} = 1.$ Given that $A$ has eigenvalues $\lambda_1=3$ and $\lambda_2=1,$ find the principal axes of the curve.
current_example.worked_solution:
Notice that $A$ is symmetric. The principal axes of the curve 

$$
\mathbf{x}^T \! A \mathbf{x} = 1
$$

are the vectors that give an orthonormal eigenvector basis for $A.$ Let's now find these eigenvectors.

- For $\lambda_1=3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-3I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-3I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/3339ed54e0188724ff3a2c3259c1c865264c9fdb3cd30d5905df3b788319dff0.svg) Dividing $\mathbf{v}_1$ by its norm $\| \mathbf{v}_1  \| = \sqrt{2},$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/05b57441a0d13f0d15daff045c515008afee8335af521ab6fbf4c9c761869105.svg)

- For $\lambda_2=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-1I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/d8e4cfb3d652955353fd9cc8f06e3db5c3f85789ed4ccf6b8e4b399f870331df.svg) Dividing $\mathbf{v}_2$ by its norm $\| \mathbf{v}_2  \| = \sqrt{2},$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/75a9653c157bafd2178568ec36dc2e373cfc6760936614a2ec4310ffdcd6f89d.svg)

Therefore, the principal axes of our curve are

$\qquad$ ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/7eee32ff96c6a34624fa0d75fb9de0904ee3a4a0c7e70635080d96518e1f2eb2.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/6d1ca42a8ac23254fdf3ec55c05cc68a65068e0f1af4383ffb3bee4d3c2e5566.svg)
